#!/bin/sh
# Nightly log backup. Bundles logs/ into a tarball and copies it to the destination.
set -eu

# Backup destination. Can be overridden by setting BACKUP_DEST in the
# environment (e.g. in the cron job / systemd unit that runs this script).
# Accepts either a local path/mount (e.g. /mnt/backups) or a remote
# host:path target (e.g. backup-host:/srv/backups), in which case rsync/scp
# is used instead of a plain copy.
DEST="${BACKUP_DEST:-/var/backups/logs}"

STAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
BUNDLE="logs-$STAMP.tar.gz"

tar -czf "$BUNDLE" logs/

case "$DEST" in
    *:*)
        # Remote destination, e.g. host:/path
        if command -v rsync >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            rsync -a "$BUNDLE" "$DEST/"
        else
            scp "$BUNDLE" "$DEST/"
        fi
        ;;
    *)
        # Local path or mounted filesystem
        mkdir -p "$DEST"
        cp "$BUNDLE" "$DEST/"
        ;;
esac

echo "wrote $BUNDLE and copied it to $DEST"

arguments.command:
chmod +x backup.sh
sh -n backup.sh && echo "syntax ok"
mkdir -p logs && echo "test log" > logs/app.log
BACKUP_DEST=/tmp/mybackups ./backup.sh
ls -la /tmp/mybackups
rm -f logs-*.tar.gz
rmdir logs 2>/dev/null || rm -rf logs
rm -rf /tmp/mybackups
